svg.title: Lockstep PP, host view
svg.desc: Lockstep PP with host, GPU and side-stream lanes per stage: every beat the host chain for the next micro-batch runs in a GPU gap after the rendezvous.
svg.text: Lockstep PP: what the host does in each beat (schematic)
The host chain that leads to launching micro-batch j (receive its control messages, build the batch, receive its activation shapes, launch) is
released only by rendezvous that complete when the previous forward ends. So it runs in a GPU gap on every stage, every beat.
Zoom: PP1 at the start of MB3. Step order from the code; the chain's width is stretched, its total is measured.
steps 1-6 (numbered below), released together at the barrier
GPU idle: the host is in steps 1–6
measured 7–11 ms per beat (PP0 15–23 ms), Fig 10 and §2
load-back j (H2D kernel): starts now, previous forward already done
released when forward j−1 ends: upstream's round-end send, downstream's receive (window 1), PP0's output ring
1 receive the relayed requests of j: blocking gloo recv, main thread
2 wait: next stage took my previous request send (window of 1)
3 bootstrap / release lists relayed from PP0, window of 1
4 build + admit j: KV pages allocated, load-back enqueued
5 blocking receive of j's activation shapes, post the NCCL receive
6 wait: next stage took my previous activation send
7 launch forward j; then block again: the early-send flush waits
for forward j-1; PP0 waits for the result 7 slots back (red curve)
Code: event_loop_pp_disagg_prefill (scheduler_pp_mixin.py) with SGLANG_PP_DECOUPLE_HOST=0: no receive inboxes, send windows of 1, results through the output ring.
host waits for a neighbour stage
host waits for its own GPU
GPU idle because the host is not done
GPU idle: waits for the slowest stage
